title: L-euro: an open protocol for digital entitlements (vouchers, coupons, tickets, discounts). Specification v0.1, draft for public comment
description:
L-euro is an open, royalty-free protocol for entitlements: rights to goods or services that are issued today as meal and social vouchers, coupons, tickets and discounts by employers, municipalities and public programmes. One data model, one lifecycle and six separable roles (issuer, payer, holder, acceptor, depositary, cover custodian) serve every programme, so an integrator implements the protocol once.

Entitlements are not money. L-euro is not e-money, not a payment system and not related to the digital euro. The depositary keeps a register of pseudonymous holder accounts and an append-only, hash-chained event log; it does not issue rights or identity attributes and does not hold the cover, which stays with a separate, replaceable cover custodian. Holders confirm a redemption by scanning the acceptor's signed QR code or NFC tag and approving it with a passkey (W3C WebAuthn); no biometric data leaves the holder's device. Settlement and EN 16931 e-invoicing receive only signed aggregates per acceptor and period, never holder accounts. Presentation from the EU Digital Identity Wallet (OpenID4VP) is a planned channel.

This release (0.1.0-draft) is a working draft for public comment, not for implementation. It contains the specification (English), JSON Schemas (draft 2020-12) and examples, governance and contribution rules, and a position paper in Bulgarian.
